message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (June 18 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day battles of the Napoleonic Wars.  While exact figures vary by source, most historians agree on the following rough totals:

| Side | Approximate casualties (killed, wounded, missing) |
|------|---------------------------------------------------|
| French & allied troops under Napoleon | ~25 000–30 000 |
| Anglo‑Dutch‑Prussian coalition under Wellington | ~20 000–25 000 |
| **Total** | ~45 000–55 000 |

These numbers include those killed, wounded, and taken prisoner or otherwise lost.  The French suffered slightly higher losses, partly because they were the attacking force and had to endure the full brunt of the Allied counter‑attacks.  The Allied side’s casualties were also significant, especially among the Prussian contingent, which suffered heavy losses during the night‑time pursuit of the retreating French.

> *Note:* Casualty estimates differ depending on how “missing” soldiers are counted and whether certain units’ losses are fully documented.  The figures above represent the consensus range found in most modern military histories of the battle.
